shortDescription: Shares of AutoNation NYSE:AN fell about 9% on Thursday after the auto retailer flagged softer service growth, affordability pressures, and a sharp decline in electric-vehicle demand at a Morgan Stanley conference, adding to a third straight session of decline.Chief Financial Officer Thomas Szlosek…

children: fell about 9% on Thursday after the auto retailer flagged softer service growth, affordability pressures, and a sharp decline in electric-vehicle demand at a Morgan Stanley conference, adding to a third straight session of decline.

Chief Financial Officer Thomas Szlosek said service growth was moderating, with third-quarter growth expected to be more modest as customers become more selective about maintenance spending. He said customer-pay service traffic remained strong, but consumers were showing more discretion on large purchases and maintenance.

expects its new-vehicle gross profit per unit to fall about 10% sequentially in the third quarter because of model-year changeover, Vice President of Investor Relations Derek Fiebig said. He added that the company was seeing affordability pressures and having to give customers more on price.
The company said its profit mix has shifted toward service and financial products, with about 80% of profit coming from those businesses and 20% from vehicle sales margins.
AutoNation Finance, meanwhile, has grown its loan portfolio to nearly $3 billion and now finances about 18% of vehicles financed through AutoNation
. Szlosek said loans held by AutoNation Finance are two to three times more profitable over their lifetime than traditional third-party financing.
EV penetration has fallen to low single digits from 8% to 9% previously after incentives expired, Szlosek said. He added that used EVs remained attractive to consumers.

title: AutoNation tumbles as service growth, affordability weigh
